learn.hook: A photo and its enlarged poster look exactly alike, only bigger — that is similarity!
points: Congruent figures have the same shape and the same size. Similar figures have the same shape but not necessarily the same size.
Two polygons with the same number of sides are similar if their corresponding angles are equal AND their corresponding sides are in the same ratio.
All circles are similar, all squares are similar and all equilateral triangles are similar.
Every pair of congruent figures is similar, but similar figures need not be congruent.
In ΔABC ~ ΔPQR the order matters: A ↔ P, B ↔ Q, C ↔ R, so AB/PQ = BC/QR = CA/RP.

example.q: ΔABC ~ ΔPQR with AB = 6 cm, BC = 8 cm and PQ = 9 cm. Find QR.
steps: Corresponding sides are in the same ratio: AB/PQ = BC/QR

learn.reallife: Maps, building models and the zoom on your phone camera all make figures similar to the real thing.

games.title: Always similar?
items: Two circles
Two squares
Two equilateral triangles
Two rectangles
Two isosceles triangles
Two rhombuses
Two right triangles
Two regular hexagons

games.title: Same shape check
items: All circles are similar.
Any circle is just a scaled copy of another.
All rectangles are similar.
A 1 × 2 rectangle and a 1 × 5 rectangle have different shapes.
Two congruent figures are always similar.
They have the same shape (scale factor 1).
Two similar figures are always congruent.
Similar figures can be of different sizes.
All rhombuses are similar.
Their angles can be different, for example a square and a thin diamond.
For two polygons to be similar, equal angles alone are always enough.
A square and a long rectangle have equal angles but are not similar. Sides must be proportional too (triangles are a special case).

quiz.q: ΔABC ~ ΔDEF with AB = 4 cm, DE = 6 cm and BC = 5 cm. What is EF?
quiz.explain: AB/DE = BC/EF, so 4/6 = 5/EF and EF = 5 × 6 ÷ 4 = 7.5 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds the difference 2 cm instead of using the ratio

quiz.q: Which pair of figures is ALWAYS similar?
quiz.explain: All squares have 90° angles and four equal sides, so one is always a scaled copy of the other.
quiz.mistake: Thinks equal angles alone make any polygons similar

quiz.q: A 10 cm × 15 cm photo is enlarged so that the 10 cm side becomes 25 cm. What does the 15 cm side become?
quiz.explain: The scale factor is 25/10 = 2.5, so the other side becomes 15 × 2.5 = 37.5 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds 15 cm to the side instead of multiplying by the scale factor

quiz.q: ΔPQR ~ ΔXYZ, with ∠P = 50° and ∠Q = 70°. What is ∠Z?
quiz.explain: ∠Z corresponds to ∠R, and ∠R = 180° − 50° − 70° = 60°.
quiz.mistake: Matches the angles in the wrong order

quiz.q: Which conditions make two polygons with the same number of sides similar?
options: Corresponding angles equal and corresponding sides in the same ratio
quiz.explain: Both conditions are needed for polygons in general: equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding sides.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one condition is always enough for any polygon

quiz.q: The scale factor from ΔABC to ΔPQR is 3. The perimeter of ΔABC is 12 cm. What is the perimeter of ΔPQR?
quiz.explain: Every side is multiplied by 3, so the perimeter is multiplied by 3: 12 × 3 = 36 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 to the perimeter or divides by 3

quiz.q: If ΔABC ~ ΔQRP, which angle is equal to ∠B?
quiz.explain: Read the letters in order: A ↔ Q, B ↔ R, C ↔ P. So ∠B = ∠R.
quiz.mistake: Matches letters by position in the alphabet instead of by order in the statement

quiz.q: On a map, 1 cm stands for 5 km. A road is 3.6 cm long on the map. How long is the real road?
quiz.explain: The map is similar to the real place with scale 1 : 5 km, so 3.6 × 5 = 18 km.
quiz.mistake: Adds 5 instead of multiplying by the scale

teach.ask: Gappu holds a small and a big photo of himself: 'Are these two pictures similar or congruent?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Same shape, maybe different size, with equal angles and sides in the same ratio. Similar!
teach.nudge: What must be the same, and what can be different, for two figures to be similar?

learn.hook: Draw a line parallel to one side of a triangle and it slices the other two sides in exactly the same ratio!
points: Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales theorem): if a line parallel to one side of a triangle meets the other two sides at distinct points, it divides those sides in the same ratio.
In ΔABC with D on AB, E on AC and DE ∥ BC: AD/DB = AE/EC.
It also follows that AD/AB = AE/AC.
Converse: if a line divides two sides of a triangle in the same ratio, it is parallel to the third side.
Special case: the line through the midpoint of one side, parallel to another side, passes through the midpoint of the third side.

example.q: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC with D on AB and E on AC. AD = 3 cm, DB = 4 cm and AE = 4.5 cm. Find EC.

learn.reallife: Carpenters making an A-frame stand fix crossbars parallel to the base; BPT tells them exactly where each bar must meet the two slanting legs.

items.text: If DE ∥ BC in ΔABC, then AD/DB = AE/___
DE ∥ BC with AD = 2, DB = 3 and AE = 4, so EC = ___
DE ∥ BC with AD = 5, AB = 15 and AE = 4, so AC = ___
If AD/DB = AE/EC, then DE is ___ to BC
A line through the midpoint of one side, parallel to a second side, meets the third side at its ___

quiz.q: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC with AD = 6 cm, DB = 9 cm and AE = 8 cm. What is EC?
quiz.explain: AD/DB = AE/EC gives 6/9 = 8/EC, so EC = 8 × 9 ÷ 6 = 12 cm.
quiz.mistake: Flips the ratio and gets 8 × 6 ÷ 9 ≈ 5.33

quiz.q: In ΔABC, D is on AB and E is on AC with AD = 3, DB = 5, AE = 4.5 and EC = 7.5. Is DE ∥ BC?
options: No, because the sides are not equal
Yes, by the converse of BPT
quiz.explain: AD/DB = 3/5 = 0.6 and AE/EC = 4.5/7.5 = 0.6. The ratios are equal, so DE ∥ BC by the converse of BPT.
quiz.mistake: Expects the pieces to be equal rather than in the same ratio

quiz.q: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC and AD/DB = 2/3. If AC = 20 cm, what is AE?
quiz.explain: AE/EC = 2/3, so AE is 2 parts out of 5 parts of AC: AE = 2/5 × 20 = 8 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses 2/3 of AC instead of 2/5

quiz.q: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC with AD = x, DB = x − 3, AE = x + 3 and EC = x − 2. Find x.
quiz.mistake: Makes a sign error when expanding (x + 3)(x − 3)

quiz.q: In ΔPQR, ST ∥ QR with S on PQ and T on PR. If PS/SQ = 3/4, what is PT/PR?
quiz.explain: PT/TR = 3/4, so PT is 3 parts of the 7 parts of PR: PT/PR = 3/7.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the part-to-part ratio with the part-to-whole ratio

quiz.q: D and E are the midpoints of AB and AC in ΔABC, and BC = 14 cm. What is DE?
quiz.explain: The segment joining the midpoints of two sides is parallel to the third side and half of it: 14 ÷ 2 = 7 cm.
quiz.mistake: Thinks DE equals BC because they are parallel

quiz.q: By what other name is the Basic Proportionality Theorem known?
quiz.explain: It is named after the Greek mathematician Thales.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names of famous theorems

quiz.q: ABCD is a trapezium with AB ∥ DC, and its diagonals meet at O. Which ratio equals AO/OC?
quiz.explain: Draw a line through O parallel to AB and DC and apply BPT in two triangles. This shows the diagonals cut each other in the same ratio: AO/OC = BO/OD.
quiz.mistake: Writes the second ratio upside down

teach.ask: Gappu draws a line across a triangle: 'When does this line cut the sides in the same ratio?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Parallel to one side means the other two sides are cut in the same ratio. Thales says hi!
teach.nudge: What must be true about the line, and what happens to the two sides it cuts?

learn.hook: You don't need to check all six parts — just the right three clues prove two triangles are similar!
points: AAA (or AA) criterion: if two angles of one triangle equal two angles of another, the triangles are similar (the third angles are then equal too).
SSS criterion: if all three pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio, the triangles are similar.
SAS criterion: if one angle is equal and the sides including that angle are in the same ratio, the triangles are similar.
For triangles, equal angles guarantee proportional sides and proportional sides guarantee equal angles.
SSA is NOT a similarity criterion. Always write the vertices in the matching order.

example.q: A girl 1.5 m tall casts a 2 m shadow. At the same time a pole casts a 12 m shadow. How tall is the pole?
steps: The sun's rays make the same angle with the ground, and both stand at 90°, so the triangles are similar (AA)

learn.reallife: Surveyors find the height of a temple tower or a tall tree using a stick and shadows — no climbing needed!

games.title: Name the criterion
pairs: All three sides in the same ratio
One equal angle with the sides around it in the same ratio
A line parallel to one side of a triangle

games.title: Similar or not?
items: If two angles of one triangle equal two angles of another, the triangles are similar.
The third angles must also match, since each triangle's angles add to 180°.
SSA is a similarity criterion.
Two sides and a non-included angle do not fix the shape.
Triangles with sides 3, 4, 5 and 6, 8, 10 are similar.
Each ratio is 2, so they are similar by SSS.
Triangles with sides 2, 3, 4 and 4, 6, 9 are similar.
If ΔABC ~ ΔDEF, then AB/DE = BC/EF = CA/FD.
Corresponding sides follow the order of the letters.
Two triangles with one pair of equal angles are always similar.
One equal angle is not enough; you need two.

quiz.q: Two triangles have sides 4, 6, 8 cm and 6, 9, 12 cm. Are they similar, and by which criterion?
quiz.explain: 6/4 = 9/6 = 12/8 = 1.5. All three sides are in the same ratio, so the triangles are similar by SSS.
quiz.mistake: Thinks sides must be equal, not just proportional

quiz.q: Meena, 1.5 m tall, casts a 2.5 m shadow. At the same time a tower casts a 40 m shadow. How tall is the tower?
quiz.explain: The triangles are similar (AA), so height/shadow is equal: 1.5/2.5 = h/40, giving h = 24 m.
quiz.mistake: Uses shadow/height on one side and height/shadow on the other

quiz.q: In ΔABC and ΔPQR, ∠A = ∠P = 40° and AB/PQ = AC/PR = 2/3. By which criterion are they similar?
quiz.explain: An equal angle (∠A = ∠P) with the sides including it in the same ratio is the SAS criterion.
quiz.mistake: Calls it SSS without having the third pair of sides

quiz.q: In ΔABC, ∠A = 65° and ∠B = 45°. In ΔDEF, ∠D = 65° and ∠F = 70°. Are the two triangles similar, and with which vertex order?
options: Only if the sides are equal
quiz.mistake: Writes the vertices in the wrong matching order

quiz.q: ΔABC ~ ΔPQR, with AB = 3 cm, BC = 4 cm, CA = 5 cm and PQ = 6 cm. What is the perimeter of ΔPQR?
quiz.explain: The scale factor is 6/3 = 2, so the perimeter is 2 × (3 + 4 + 5) = 24 cm.
quiz.mistake: Gives the perimeter of ΔABC

quiz.q: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC with D on AB and E on AC. AD = 2 cm, AB = 6 cm and DE = 3 cm. What is BC?
quiz.explain: ΔADE ~ ΔABC by AA (corresponding angles are equal). So DE/BC = AD/AB = 2/6, giving BC = 3 × 6 ÷ 2 = 9 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses AD/DB = 2/4 instead of AD/AB

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a criterion for similarity of triangles?
quiz.explain: Two sides and an angle that is not between them do not fix the shape of a triangle.
quiz.mistake: Assumes any three parts are enough

quiz.q: In right ΔABC with ∠B = 90°, BD is drawn perpendicular to AC. Which triangle is ΔADB similar to?
quiz.explain: In ΔADB and ΔABC, ∠A is common and ∠ADB = ∠ABC = 90°. By AA, A ↔ A, D ↔ B, B ↔ C, so ΔADB ~ ΔABC.
quiz.mistake: Gets the order of the matching vertices wrong

teach.ask: Gappu has two triangles: 'Do I have to measure everything to know they are similar?'
teach.praise: Tweet tweet! AA, SSS or SAS — any one of these clues is enough. Detective Gappu is ready!
teach.nudge: What are the three shortcuts, and do sides need to be equal or just in the same ratio?
